title: OpenScreening
synopsis:
ATA’s free community film/video show welcomes short format work or (15 min or less) from all genres. An open forum for independent filmmakers to show their work, we hold screenings the first Thursday of the month at 8:00 pm. Entries must be received by 7:00 pm on show night.
Submissions: To submit a digital file, email openscreening@atasite.org. For physical media, label all tapes with name, contact info, title, and length, and mail to: Open Screening, 992 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110. 1–2 weeks advance submissions recommended. If not, just walk in before the show.
Maximum length: 15 min.
Formats: Digital file (PC or Mac), DVD, miniDV/DV-cam, VHS, beta, 8 mm, and 16 mm. For 8 mm and 16 mm films give us advance notice.
Doors at 7:30 pm, show at 8:00 pm, FREE

title: Other Cinema: Incredibly Strange Music
synopsis: Here’s an aggressive critical engagement with both old and new pop-rhetorical tropes, led by legendary beatnik re-mixer 99 Hooker! His much-anticipated appearance here promises both wise and wise-guy versions of the comtempo sub-pop-music scene, as well as genius patter in situ. Avatar Pit, his real-time media delirium, is supported fore and aft by a raft of utterly anomalous musical singularities—spontaneous musique concrete sessions, damaged polka fragments, Troloman, Babalu, the Blob, the Residents, Eric Burden and the Animals, Chrissie Hynde and the Pretenders…rockin hard! AND Liberace, Spike Jones, the Mirror Man, Louis Prima & Keely Smith, singing ostriches, and so many Other outsiders, now centerstage in 99‘s upside-down musical universe!! $14

title: Other Cinema: Shapeshifters Benefit
synopsis:
MAGICK~REALISM~PSYCHO ~GEOGRAPHY
A colossal collab…of microcinemas!! Other Cinema takes a knee to Oakland‘s SHAPESHIFTERS project, with a party-hardy program of Bay Area magick! Anchoring the Psycho-Geo line-up is none Other than stage magician extraordinaire Michael Nguyen, and his bunny Houdini! This master’s mind-blowing visual delights are then answered by very different versions of “reality”, local verite and archival lovelies bearing on our shared space and sensibility: Playland, Berkeley mudflats, DIY solar ovens, Bullitt production shorts, James Hong‘s cine-poems, sidewalk-busking DJ Beau Dayshus, and the Bay Area premiere of Bill Morrison‘s Sawyer Ave, Sunday Afternoon. AND on sale: Not only Maya‘s charm bracelets, but also GILBERT‘s CRAFT BEER! $9-$99
